points.description: States that the height of a tree is a length (or the number of edges/nodes) of a path — i.e. height is defined in terms of a path, not just a count of nodes or levels. Equivalent Tamil/English wording accepted.
States that the path begins at the root of the tree.
States that the path ends at a leaf (a node with no children). Saying 'any leaf' or 'a leaf node' is acceptable.
States that the height is the longest (maximum) such path — i.e. the longest path from the root to a leaf, taken over all root-to-leaf paths.
points.partial_credit: Half marks if the answer says the path is long/deep but does not make clear it is the maximum over all root-to-leaf paths.

levels.says: Says the path should be long or the deepest path, but does not state it is the longest/maximum among all root-to-leaf paths.

rubric.notes: Full marks require all four ideas: height is a path length, the path starts at the root, it ends at a leaf, and it is the longest such path. The 'longest' idea carries the most weight (2 marks); an answer that only says 'a long path' earns half of that point. An answer that gives only a vague statement such as 'the depth of the tree' with no root, leaf or longest-path detail earns little or no credit.
